items.title: Joseph Thomas Interview, 1960-09-29
items.q: The interviewee responds to the interviewer's story about Slowdrag by saying 'Yeah, no, they used to play it down by the old mill stream, I remember that.' The interviewee confirms the activity (playing with a broomstick) but does not claim personal interaction with Slowdrag, only knowledge of the p

ctx.x: Well, they were. I've heard them played lately, the numbers that my dad and mother and them used to sing and play. Yeah, they used to play them lately. Did they sing and play any hymns in your home? Well, no, it wasn't much, not much on hymns. You see, uh, no, they didn't play with the, you know, everybody was drinking, so I guess they didn't want to mix no hymns with liquor. Drinking and talking and laughing and then playing these tunes.

That time I heard Slowdrag, his wife had a little quartet there. They were playing some hymns, you know, she sings and plays in a church. Yeah. They were, they were using all hymns that night that I heard them. Uh-huh. And Slowdrag was using the broom. I just wondered if they might have had that in your home, too.

Yeah, no, they used to play it down by the old mill stream, I remember that. Yeah. And, oh, quite a few numbers, but, you know, it'd take time for them to come to it, you know. Oh, yeah. Sure. But, uh, they used to make good music with that kind of singing and that stick, or that broomstick for the bass.
